title: What total does a mean of one hundred thirty four give?
description: A set of fifteen values has a mean of one hundred and thirty four. The mean shares the total equally, so multiplying the mean by the number of values gives the sum of the data.
teaching_notes: One idea: the sum of the data equals the mean times the number of values. Watch for students who divide the mean by the number of values instead.

source: Figure it Out (mean and median, question 8)
video_script.why: A child who can find a mean from a total now turns a mean back into a total.
video_script.substitution: the book's set of 15 values with mean 134
video_script.anchor: fifteen equal piles, each labelled with the mean 134
video_script.payoff_line: The sum of the data is two thousand and ten

final_answer.spoken: the sum of the data is two thousand and ten

never_show: 134 ÷ 15 as the sum, marked as right
video_script.design: One set of fifteen equal piles all video, each pile holding the mean. The piles are counted into one big total, and the total is shared back into piles for the check.

marks.given: the number of values and the mean are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, there are fifteen values and the mean is one hundred and thirty four.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sum of the data

marks.find: the words the sum of the data are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the sum of all fifteen values.

marks.rule: sum = mean × number of values is written

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, use the sum as the mean multiplied by the number of values.
<bookmark mark='put'/>That is one hundred and thirty four times fifteen.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Step two, split fifteen into ten and five. One hundred and thirty four times ten is one thousand three hundred and forty.
<bookmark mark='five'/>One hundred and thirty four times five is six hundred and seventy.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Add them, and the total is two thousand and ten.

marks.share: 2010 is shared into fifteen equal piles
marks.back: each pile reads 134, the mean in the book

narration: <bookmark mark='share'/>Check the result by sharing the total back into fifteen equal piles.
<bookmark mark='back'/>Two thousand and ten divided by fifteen is one hundred and thirty four, the mean we started with.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The sum of the data is two thousand and ten.
